rfm_tuples.R: Occupancy in our office portfolio decreased from 88.9% as of December 31, 2023 to 87.1% as of December 31, 2024. We expect average occupancy in our office portfolio to range from 85.0% to 86.5% for 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution between 2024-02-06 10-K (FY23) and 2025-02-11 10-K (FY24), plus 2025-04-29 Q1 10-Q occupancy print; check whether actual Q1 occupancy already breaches the guidance lower bound.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Occupancy trajectory FY22 90.7% -> FY23 89.2% (avg, 88.8% spot) -> FY24 88.0% (avg, 87.1% spot) -> Q1 2025 85.5% spot. Q1 2025 10-Q lowered the FY25 high-end of the guide from 86.5% to 86.0% (75bps cut) just 11 weeks after the 10-K. Q1 2025 actual (85.5%) is already INSIDE the bottom half of the original 85.0-86.5% band with three quarters left to run. Same property NOI was -2.3% YoY in Q1 2025 and management explicitly guides to lower NOI for the remainder of 2025.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K guidance band (85.0-86.5%) was set 75 days after year-end and was already eroding by the Q1 print. Management is honest about the direction but the guide proved optimistic on first observation. 88.9% -> 85.5% in 15 months is a 340 bps fall in a SunBelt-centric REIT — disclosed but trending poorly.

rfm_tuples.R: As part of ongoing efforts to reduce waste, the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) are reaching out to all tenant agencies with non-firm term leases to see if there are opportunities to reduce space usage. We currently have 30 leases with 23 different agencies of the Federal government across five different markets, which encompass an aggregate of 737,000 square feet.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — DOGE/GSA disclosure is NEW in this 10-K (not in FY23 10-K). Cross-check (a) prevalence of 'non-firm term leases' wording across EDGAR 10-Ks via edgar_fts; (b) verify the Federal Government total revenue and remaining lease term from the Customers table.
rfm_tuples.M_value: edgar_fts FTS shows 'non-firm term leases' has 1 hit in EDGAR 10-Ks pre-cutoff (HIW only); 'Department of Government Efficiency' has 98 10-K hits — HIW is one of the early disclosers. Prior FY23 10-K contains NO mention of DOGE or non-firm term lease risk; this is freshly added 2024 risk language. Customers table: Federal Government is the #4 customer at 736,663 sf, $21.12M annual GAAP rent (2.64%), weighted average remaining term only 4.0 years — the SHORTEST WALT in the top-5 (vs Bank of America 9.2yr, Asurion 11.8yr, Met Life 6.2yr, Bridgestone 12.7yr).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — management discloses the DOGE risk but soft-pedals: the Federal Government is a top-5 customer with the SHORTEST remaining lease term (4.0 years) and a meaningful chunk of those 30 leases will be the focus of GSA's space-reduction push. 2.64% of revenue plus knock-on signaling risk to other downsizers is non-trivial for a name already losing occupancy.

rfm_tuples.R: We are currently in compliance with financial covenants and other requirements with respect to our consolidated debt. Although we expect to remain in compliance with these covenants and ratios for at least the next year, depending upon our future operating performance, property and financing transactions and general economic conditions, we cannot provide any assurances that we will continue to be in compliance.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check covenant language for any softening between 2024-02-06 10-K and 2025-02-11 10-K, and 2025-04-29 Q1 10-Q. Verify debt maturity wall and refinancing exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Covenant-compliance language unchanged across 10-K FY23 -> 10-K FY24 -> Q1 2025 10-Q (still boilerplate 'currently in compliance' + 'cannot provide any assurances'). Debt maturity wall: ZERO principal due 2025, but $207M in 2026, $458.8M in 2027, $802.8M in 2028, $517.2M in 2029. Weighted avg cost of fixed debt 4.31%, variable 5.33%. The Feb 2034 notes priced at 7.65% (issued mid-2024) reveal current market refi cost ~3-5 percentage points above the legacy debt stack. Revolver was modified in Q1 2024 to extend to Jan 2028. Q1 2025: $145M revolver balance, $599.9M available — adequate near-term liquidity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Covenants and short-term liquidity are honestly disclosed and currently adequate. The forensic concern is forward refi: $1.26B of debt rolls 2027-2028 at current ~7.6% market rates vs ~4.3% legacy book — significant FFO drag once it lands, but not a 12-month issue.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, only Bank of America (3.8%) and Asurion (3.5%) accounted for more than 3% of our annualized GAAP revenues. ... Our 20 largest customers account for a meaningful portion of our revenues.

summary: HIW is a transparently-disclosed SunBelt office REIT showing real cyclical operating headwinds but no honesty-framework red flags. The two MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY tuples are (1) FY25 occupancy guidance already eroding in Q1 print (high-end cut 50bps to 86.0% with actual already at 85.5%), and (2) DOGE/GSA non-firm-term-lease overhang on a #4 customer (Federal Government, 2.64% rev, 4.0yr WALT — shortest in top-5) — both fully disclosed but management framing is mildly optimistic vs the trajectory. All other forensic tests PASS: Deloitte auditor since 2006 with no Item 4.01 events; zero going-concern language; insider activity is routine 10b5-1 only (no CEO/CFO open-market sales despite drawdown); covenants compliant with adequate near-term liquidity ($599.9M revolver headroom + $34M cash); single FY24 impairment was confined to a non-core Pittsburgh asset, not the SunBelt core; no counterparty-mirror distress signals in EDGAR FTS. Material forward risk is the 2027-2028 debt maturity wall ($1.26B at ~7.6% current refi rates vs 4.3% legacy book) and the cyclical occupancy slide, but neither constitutes the lying/obscuring pattern the framework is designed to detect.
